truths.CP2:
WITH promo_products AS (
  -- one row per promotion that started in Q3 2025 and product in it
  SELECT p.promo_id, pp.product_id, p.start_date, p.end_date
  FROM promotions AS p
  JOIN promotion_products AS pp ON pp.promo_id = p.promo_id
  WHERE p.start_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-07-01' AND DATE '2025-09-30'
),
zero_weeks AS (
  -- one row per promotion and product with at least one baseline week of no units
  SELECT x.promo_id, x.product_id
  FROM promo_products AS x
  JOIN weekly_units AS w ON w.product_id = x.product_id
  WHERE w.week_start >= x.start_date - INTERVAL 28 DAY
    AND w.week_start < x.start_date
    AND w.units = 0
  GROUP BY x.promo_id, x.product_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM zero_weeks
truths.CP4:
WITH promo_products AS (
  -- one row per promotion that started in Q3 2025 and product in it
  SELECT p.promo_id, pp.product_id, p.start_date, p.end_date
  FROM promotions AS p
  JOIN promotion_products AS pp ON pp.promo_id = p.promo_id
  WHERE p.start_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-07-01' AND DATE '2025-09-30'
),
weekly_averages AS (
  -- one row per promotion and product
  SELECT x.promo_id, x.product_id,
         AVG(CASE WHEN w.week_start >= x.start_date - INTERVAL 28 DAY
                   AND w.week_start < x.start_date THEN w.units END) AS baseline_units_wk,
         AVG(CASE WHEN w.week_start BETWEEN x.start_date AND x.end_date THEN w.units END) AS promo_units_wk
  FROM promo_products AS x
  JOIN weekly_units AS w ON w.product_id = x.product_id
  GROUP BY x.promo_id, x.product_id
)
SELECT ROUND(MAX(100.0 * (promo_units_wk - baseline_units_wk) / NULLIF(baseline_units_wk, 0)), 1)
FROM weekly_averages

CP1.explanation: A week with no sales is part of the product's normal pattern, so it counts as 0; leaving it out raises the baseline and shrinks the uplift.

CP5.explanation: A promotion worked only once cannibalisation, the dip after it, other events and the margin after the discount are checked; calling every extra unit new demand or picking the most flattering baseline overstates it.
